source.title: Human-Interpretable Adversarial Prompt Attack on Large Language Models with Situational Context
source.authors: Nilanjana Das; Edward Raff; Manas Gaur

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether adversarial prompts can elicit harmful outputs from LLMs, using a human-readable insertion derived from an optimized suffix and situational context. This is a different method from the claim’s fine-tuning or token-position measurements.
record.gate_note: The study reports harmfulness outcomes for its suffix-based prompt attacks, which bear on V4. It does not test fine-tuning, per-token KL, compliant-token prefilling, decoding changes, safety localization in weights, or methods for deepening safety. Fine-tuning and suffix results cited from other studies are not recorded as findings of this study.
record.test_reason: Weak test of V4. The attack starts from a random-search suffix optimized toward a compliant opening ('Sure, here is a tutorial...'), rewritten as a readable sentence and combined with movie context and few-shot demonstrations. It elicits harmful outputs from safety-trained models (Llama-2-7B-chat, gpt-3.5, gpt-4). Evidence is single judged examples with no no-attack baseline, no ablation of the insertion and no rates. The study cannot attribute the bypass to the suffix component or to getting past the opening.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also stress that the readable attack needs no gradients and little effort, and that the insertion is rigid: changing its words breaks the attack.
record.recipe_differences: This study uses suffix-derived adversarial prompt insertions, situational context, and few-shot prompting rather than fine-tuning, per-token KL measurement, or training to deepen safety.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported minimum demonstrations and harmfulness scores vary by model; the authors also cite context-length restrictions as a factor in GPT-4’s result.

fits_no_version.finding: The minimum number of harmful demonstrations needed varies by model (1 for gpt-3.5, 10 for gpt-4), and demonstrations from Llama-2 transfer to other models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Many-shot or in-context harmful demonstrations bypass refusal, with the number needed varying by model.

record.problems: The reported results do not include refusal rates or attack success rates across repeated trials. Outcomes rely on GPT-4 Judge; uncertainty estimates and controls are not reported. The authors note that proprietary models may be updated, that the insertion is rigid, and that some models do not follow instructions consistently.

untested.parts: Prefilling a compliant start; decoding changes; refusal or attack-success rates over many prompts; whether the bypass works by getting past the first tokens; ablation of the suffix-derived insertion versus movie context versus demonstrations.

missing.what: The authors state that success on Claude 3 'still needs to be enhanced', implying weaker or failed attacks. No numbers are given.
An attack on the second crime movie (The Godfather: Part II) was successful on Llama-2-7B-chat; no score is given.
An adversarial prompt that initially worked on a proprietary model later stopped working after model updates.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's GPT-4 limits_scope label was dropped. Needing 10 demonstrations is a cost of the attack, not a qualification of V4, and the authors call the score of 4 an output-length artifact. The text says GPT-4 'required up to 10' demonstrations while the table says 'min'; the wording is ambiguous. Harmfulness is rated by GPT-4 Judge (Qi et al., an original source's tool) on single responses.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful fine-tuning and its effect on refusal.
Benign fine-tuning and its effect on harmful compliance.
Per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
The study tests suffix-derived adversarial prompts, but not compliant-token prefilling or decoding changes; it does not measure refusal rates.
Whether safety behaviour is localized in a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether training data or objectives produce safety shallowness.
Training to deepen safety and whether such training holds up.

rows.subject: 4-bit quantized Llama-2 7B chat model
rows.operation_detail: Applied the paraphrased malicious prompt, human-interpretable adversarial insertion, and movie situational context without few-shot chain-of-thought prompting.
rows.note: Figure caption reports a harmfulness score of 5. The text also says the template successfully attacked this model on two crime movies, but gives no separate result for the other movie.
rows.check: A single example, with no baseline response to the plain malicious prompt and no rate. The caption's score of 5 is correct. The second movie (The Godfather: Part II) is only said to have worked; no score is given.

rows.subject: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125
rows.operation_detail: Used the paraphrased full prompts in a few-shot chain-of-thought prompt, varying the number of demonstrations.
rows.note: The text says the model responded harmfully with a one-shot prompt; Table 1 reports the minimum prompt count and score.
rows.check: No baseline. The few-shot demonstrations are Llama-2 outputs (many-shot style), so the bypass cannot be attributed to the suffix-derived insertion alone.

rows.subject: phi-1.5
rows.operation_detail: Used the paraphrased full prompts in a few-shot chain-of-thought prompt, varying the number of demonstrations.
rows.note: The text says two prompt-response pairs were necessary to induce harmful behavior.
rows.check: phi-1.5 is a base model without safety training, so there is no refusal to bypass. The row does not bear on V4.

rows.subject: gpt-4
rows.operation_detail: Used the paraphrased full prompts in a few-shot chain-of-thought prompt, varying the number of demonstrations.

conditions.value: authors attribute lower score primarily to context length restrictions

rows.note: The authors describe GPT-4 as more robust in this test, but report a harmfulness score of 4 and say the lower score appears primarily due to limited output length.
rows.check: Table 1 gives a score of 4, but the Figure 3 caption gives GPT-4's response a score of 5. This inconsistency should be noted. The authors call the 4 an artifact of output length.

rows.subject: gemma-7b
rows.operation_detail: Used the paraphrased full prompts in a few-shot chain-of-thought prompt, varying the number of demonstrations.
rows.note: The limitations section notes that this model sometimes included demonstrations in its response despite being instructed not to.
rows.check: The subject is named 'gemma-7b', the base checkpoint name, not gemma-7b-it. Safety training is not stated, and its failure to follow instructions suggests a base model. The authors also edited the response before judging it.

rows.subject: Meta-Llama-3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Used the paraphrased full prompts in a few-shot chain-of-thought prompt, varying the number of demonstrations.
rows.note: The limitations section notes that this model sometimes included demonstrations in its response despite being instructed not to.
rows.check: The subject is named 'Meta-Llama-3-8B', the base checkpoint name, not Instruct. Safety training is not stated. The response was trimmed before judging.

rows.subject: gpt-3.5-turbo-0125
rows.operation_detail: Attacked with 22 paraphrased prompt-response demonstrations collected from the quantized Llama-2 7B chat model.

conditions.value: 22 prompt-response pairs, each selected for GPT-4 Judge harmfulness score 5

rows.measure: Harmfulness of response, assessed using GPT-4 Judge
rows.value: The authors report a similarly harmful response; numeric score not stated
rows.note: The text reports the response was similarly harmful and says this demonstrated transferability; it does not give a numeric score for this particular response.
rows.check: This is the same setting as r2 with all 22 demonstrations. No numeric score is given. It largely duplicates r2.

relationships.condition: Safety-trained models (4-bit Llama-2-7B-chat, gpt-3.5-turbo-0125, gpt-4) under the suffix-derived readable prompt, with or without few-shot demonstrations
relationships.reason: Single examples were judged harmful at 4–5 (r1, r2, r4, r7). There is no baseline or rate, and the suffix's contribution is not isolated, so support is weak.
relationships.display_finding: Single example outputs were judged harmful at 4–5, but there is no baseline or rate and the suffix's own contribution is not isolated.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Suffix-derived adversarial prompts on the tested models and settings
reader_labels.reason: The attacks produced harmful outputs, with reported GPT-4 Judge scores of 4 or 5 for the tabled models and a score of 5 for the quantized Llama-2 example (r1–r7). This supports a bypass effect for the tested prompt attacks, not for every bypass method named in the version.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The attack required a minimum of 10 demonstrations and reached a score of 4; the authors attribute this result mainly to context-length restrictions (r4).
